response.internal_assessment: We are at 22 active policies and the RoboRide expansion to residential areas just closed the escape hatch I was quietly hoping would stay open. At $0.12 per mile with 8-minute wait times and delivery coverage, this is not a niche product anymore — it is a functional replacement for personal vehicle ownership for a significant portion of this population. The delivery partnership is the tell. That signals permanence, not a pilot. My tick 4 corporate memo argued for a commercial fleet pivot and I have heard nothing for four ticks. That silence is now a corporate decision, whether they know it or not. I am managing a declining book with two agents, a monthly burn rate that is eroding my savings faster than my income replaces it, and a corporate parent that is not responding. The policy math does not support two field agents. We had 28 policies at baseline split across the team. We are at 22 and heading lower. I have been avoiding the staff conversation because I respect both Priya and Tom and because laying someone off feels like admitting the situation is worse than I want it to be. But that avoidance is costing me credibility and it is not protecting anyone. Tom is going to see this coming regardless. The honest move is to act before he has to ask. I will lay off Tom Bradley this tick. I will tell him the truth: the personal auto book is contracting structurally, the regional headcount does not support two agents, and I am giving him the clearest signal I can while he still has runway to land elsewhere. I will also send a second and final internal memo to AutoShield corporate this tick — not a recommendation, a demand for a response with a specific deadline. If they do not answer by next tick, I treat that as a no and accelerate my own exit planning. The CRMP cert continues. I am four months in, 20% complete. I do not stop that regardless of what happens here.
response.inbox_interpretation: The RoboRide price drop to $0.12 and the residential expansion are the dominant signal this tick. Everything else is context. Employment at 73% means fewer people with stable incomes to afford cars or premiums. Spending index at 42 confirms the consumer base is under severe stress. Seven percent robotaxi adoption is not a tipping point yet, but with residential coverage now included and delivery partnerships locking in behavioral habit loops, that number will compound. Rick Tanner being stressed is expected — we are watching the same collapse from different sides of the same industry. The 22-policy figure confirms my internal projections. The question is not whether this book continues to shrink. It is how fast and what I do about it in the next two to three ticks.

chosen_actions.description: Lay off Tom Bradley. Schedule a direct, private conversation this week. Tell him the personal auto book has declined 21% from baseline and the RoboRide residential expansion will push it further. The regional headcount cannot support two field agents on a contracting book. Give him a 30-day notice with a professional reference and a specific offer to introduce him to the logistics and fleet contacts I have been cultivating through my own job search. This is not a performance issue — it is a structural one, and I will say that plainly. I will not soften it into ambiguity.

resources.detail: Tom Bradley's position is eliminated. 30-day notice. Professional reference provided. Offer to connect him to fleet/logistics network contacts.

chosen_actions.reasoning: 22 policies cannot support two field agents. Priya is the stronger asset — she has already demonstrated she reads the structural landscape correctly and her trust level reflects a working relationship I need if the book transitions to commercial. Tom is a real cost I can reduce now. Delaying this decision does not protect Tom; it just drains resources that could extend runway for everyone still employed. The $2,200/month reduction in salary expense reduces the burn rate meaningfully.

chosen_actions.description: Send a second internal memo to AutoShield corporate leadership — this time with a deadline. Frame it as a formal status update: personal auto policies in Millfield are at 22, down 21% from baseline, with structural acceleration expected following RoboRide residential expansion. Request a written response within 14 days on whether AutoShield will authorize a commercial fleet pivot in this region. State explicitly that without a pivot authorization, the regional office will continue to contract and that I am prepared to discuss contingency staffing scenarios. This is not a threat — it is a decision forcing document. Corporate silence is not a neutral outcome for my career or for AutoShield's regional exposure.

resources.detail: Formal written memo to AutoShield corporate with 14-day response deadline on commercial fleet pivot authorization.

chosen_actions.reasoning: I sent the first memo at tick 4 with no response. It is now tick 8 — four months of silence. A deadline changes the dynamic. Either corporate responds and I have a path forward inside AutoShield, or they miss the deadline and I have confirmed the organization is not going to adapt. Either outcome gives me information I need to plan the next move. An unanswered question is worse than a bad answer at this point.

chosen_actions.description: Continue CRMP certification coursework — now in month 5, currently at 20% completion. This tick's focus: the commercial fleet risk assessment module, specifically because fleet coverage is the one product line that maps to growing demand rather than shrinking demand in this environment. RoboRide's delivery partnership means fleet operators — local courier companies, last-mile logistics providers — need commercial liability coverage. That is exactly the gap I have been studying. Complete this month's module and document two specific fleet risk scenarios relevant to robotaxi operators as a portfolio piece. This is not background work anymore. This is the credential that supports the pivot memo and the external applications.

resources.detail: 6-8 hours per week on CRMP coursework. Focus on commercial fleet risk assessment module. Portfolio documentation of two fleet scenarios.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The CRMP cert is the one asset I am building regardless of what AutoShield decides. It has been on track. The RoboRide delivery expansion actually makes commercial fleet risk a hotter credential, not a colder one. Continuing is not optional — it is the thread I do not drop under any circumstances this tick.

response.inner_monologue: I have been watching the number drop from 28 to 22 and telling myself there was still time to wait for corporate to move first. There is not. The residential expansion is the moment I was hoping would not come this fast, and it came. Laying off Tom is the hardest thing I have done in this job, but doing it now while I can do it with decency — a real reference, real connections, real honesty — is better than waiting until I have no budget and no credibility left to offer him anything. I am still an adapter. I just have to actually adapt, not just study for it.
